note: For every product item: the lowest level it belongs to, the module it is shown under, who it applies to, and any per-level quantity rule that differs from the item's own `qty`. Rules: basis and factor as in products/SCHEMA.md; `days` fixes the number of days; `less_days` leaves out days already covered by another item; `unit` forces the pack size to 1. `optional` items are shown but kept out of totals and progress. A `qty` here replaces the item's own quantity rule at every level; `rule` gives the words printed beside the number. Audience tags (`only.has`) are those in data/actions/SCHEMA.md. `alternative` marks a product that can be bought in place of others in its group (the combination smoke and CO alarm): it is shown beside them with its picks, has no tick box and stays out of totals and progress.

qty.rule: 2 for each adult or teenager aged 14 or over: both in the grab bag. A younger child's bag has its own small bottle

1 pack of 3,600 kcal for each person aged 6 or over: about 1,200 kcal a day for 3 days, which is not a full diet. The case of 12 meals is counted as one for every four people, at one meal a day each. A younger child gets food they already eat, not ration bars
6 for each adult or teenager aged 14 or over (this site's assumption: 2 a day for 3 smoky days), bought in whole packs. No respirator is counted for a younger child
1 for each adult or teenager aged 14 or over; add one for each younger child old enough to wear one
1 for each adult or teenager aged 14 or over, one for each phone. Add one for a younger child who carries a phone
1 for each person aged 1 or over who normally rides in the car
1 for each pet. All three picks are dog harnesses: for a cat, buy a harness made for cats instead, as a backup to the carrier
1 tray for each cat, sold in packs of 4 or 5; dogs need none

2.rule: Sealed water for 3 days: 1 gallon for each person a day, plus half a gallon for each pet (this site's assumption, sized for a dog)

3.rule: Sealed water for the first 3 days only: 1 gallon for each person a day, plus half a gallon for each pet (this site's assumption, sized for a dog). Your own containers hold the rest of two weeks (rigid water containers)

1.rule: 1 pack to split between the grab bags (this site's suggestion)

3.rule: At two weeks too, bags for the first 3 days only: one bag per use, 5 uses a day for each person who uses the toilet. After day 3 the bucket, liners and absorbent take over (X5-05)

2.rule: 1 can for the household at a 3-day target

3.rule: 5 gallons of can for each person for each week of your target (Oregon's planning figure), which is 10 gallons each at two weeks; the count follows the size of can you pick

qty.rule: 1 for each person aged 6 or over, and never fewer than 1 for the household. An adult cleans a younger child's hands, and the bottle stays out of a small child's reach
2 for the household: one by the front door and one by the bed. Add one for the car kit if you have a car

qty.note: Count the cells in every light and radio you own and keep twice that number spare. The price shown is for one pack

qty.rule: One outside each sleeping area and one on each level of the home, unless a combination smoke and CO alarm already covers that spot. Count your own. The price shown is for one alarm

An alternative, not an extra. One outside each sleeping area and one on each level of the home, in place of a separate smoke alarm and CO alarm there; bedrooms still need their own smoke alarms. Count your own, then subtract the working alarms already there. The price shown is for one alarm

One inside each bedroom. Outside each sleeping area and on each level you need smoke protection too, from a smoke alarm or from a combination smoke and CO alarm, which does both jobs. Count your own rooms, then subtract the working alarms already there. The price shown is for one alarm
1 for the kitchen side of the home; in a house, add one for each other floor
2 for the household: one in the fridge and one in the freezer. Add a third for the cooler if you keep one for food or medicine (X3-10, X7-02)

2.rule: 1 container to start with, so you can learn to clean, fill and date it (this site's suggestion). 72 hours at home's three days are covered by sealed water

qty.rule: 1 bucket toilet for the household. Add a second lidded 5-gallon bucket for pee (U5-19, X5-05); this count does not include it

3.rule: 1 liner for each person who uses the toilet, for each day after the first 3 (the bag kits cover those); the number is how many boxes or cases that takes

About 1 cup of dry cover for each person who uses the toilet, for each day after the first 3 (this site's estimate). The number is how many bags or tubs that takes, from the person-days on each pick's size line

qty.note: One supply for each person who menstruates, teenagers included. The site does not ask who menstruates, so count for yourself; the price shown is for one supply

qty.rule: 1 for each person aged 1 or over. A baby gets no sleeping bag: a sleep surface of their own
Optional: at most 1, on the wall near the kitchen door. A pan lid by the stove comes first.

explain.stored-water: 72 hours at home covers the first three days with sealed store-bought water, which needs no cleaning or rotation. Two weeks at home covers the remaining days in refillable containers you fill from the tap.
explain.toilet: 72 hours at home covers three days with one-use bag-and-gel kits in your own toilet bowl. Two weeks at home adds a bucket toilet with plain heavy liners and absorbent for the remaining days, which costs far less per day.
